note: The RUNTIME law of the navbar example picker, declared as data. `📚️example-picker.json` (🛂️manifest) says WHICH examples one surface may offer; this says what picking one MUST do. One row is one pick on a live surface: the flow window must republish exactly the picked example's authored widget ids, no widget of the example before it may survive, every attached preview window's evaluation chain must be re-armed by the gesture itself, and the preview's retained evaluation must stop being the previous example's. The empty id is the picker's own `No example` row (`NavbarExampleSelect` normalizes its `__none__` sentinel to `""`), and it CLEARS the graph — a label that promises no example must not silently load one. Language-agnostic: an implementation in any language replays these picks and answers the same published/retired/armed lists.

viewer.note: The read-only surface has NO flow window to republish, so a pick is measured by the graph its VIEWED document reports — `interaction_topology`, the very resolution the preview render and the `flowEvalTick` chain run. Three picker states, not two: an implementation that cannot tell `never picked` from `picked No example` cannot satisfy this table.

states.why: Nothing has been picked, so the surface shows the document this session opened. This is the ABSENCE of a `setActiveExample` dispatch, never an empty one.

The picker's own `No example` row, whose `__none__` sentinel `NavbarExampleSelect` normalizes to the empty id. It CLEARS, exactly as the sibling surface's own row does. Collapsing it onto `never-picked` made it resolve to the opened document — which in the playground IS a bundled example — so the row painted the hexagonal mushroom column's three meshes (`meshesLen 3641`, measured on the served viewer 2026-09-13, `🗑️generated/viewer-status/parity-1/results.json`).
A named example projects over the opened document without mutating it: a viewer owns no write authority, so the pick lives on its own config lane.

rows.why: A fresh editor instance opens the plugin's default document, and the picker's value is the example that document IS.

Boot #11 of `📓️runtime-verification-2026-09-09.md`: the picker label changed to Box Shell Preview while the flow window kept the hexagonal-mushroom-column node ids and no fault appeared anywhere. The switch owes both windows its own consequence, never a host refresh's.

`size` and `box` exist in BOTH examples with different parameters, so an id-keyed survivor check would pass on a graph that still holds the previous example's fillet chain. Only the exact published set is the answer.
Each preview window owns its own retained evaluation publication, so the switch owes each one a restart — and owes each exactly one (`🔒️tick-latch.json`).

`NavbarExampleSelect`'s `No example` row dispatches `setActiveExample` with an empty id. Resolving that to the app's DEFAULT document loaded the hexagonal mushroom column — itself a bundled example — so the row silently did the opposite of what it says (measured live 2026-09-12: `setActiveExample {exampleId: }` settled with one config upsert and zero artifact mutations, and the column stayed on screen).
The picker can only ever offer declared ids, so an id it never published is a no-op rather than a blanked graph — and it owes no re-arm, because nothing about the evaluation moved.
